newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank sells T-bills to drain liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank sells T-bills to drain liquidity.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said it was offering to sell state treasury bills from its portfolio to drain liquidity from the market.
The NBS said in a statement it was offering unspecified tranches of six- and 70-day T-bills at undisclosed rates.
"We are offering these T-bills, and we leave it on banks to decide on the volume thay want to buy," Peter Andresic, head of the NBS Open Market Operation Department, told Reuters.
He said the central bank was concluding individual deals with commercial banks, It would not disclose rates or announce volumes sold.
One Bratislava-based money market dealer said the NBS was accepting around a 17 percent rate for six-day T-bills.
The average rate in the NBS one-week repo tender on Wednesday fell to 15.55 percent from 16.30 percent in a similar repo on Tuesday.
The central bank said earlier it would not hold any refinancing repo tenders on Thursday as the local banking sector appeared to have enough crown liquidity to meet minimum reserve requirements.
According to NBS figures, the Slovak banking sector as of July 30 fulfilled its minimum reserve requirements 100 percent.
The daily volume of minimum reserves for commercial banks totals 36.583 billion crowns in the current reserves period ending July 31.
